fol.notes: Agreement as the subject's grammatical_number (enum Number): the sentence choice is a find on it, each candidate sentence a surface of its number in 'choices'. The rule over the class is a finite quantifier over the record's subjects. Fact ids follow the DL file. Delete: the class link to the wider rule is cut in every world (top-level gives_up), as in the DL file; a phrase stored whole keeps its form through stores.

wider_rule.says: A subject that is not plural (a singular or mass noun phrase, or a clause) takes a singular verb (anchored by countless instances).
wider_rule.z3: All(s, [snorving, dramping, smoking, parting], Implies(non_plural(s), grammatical_number(s) == singular))

class_link.says: A gerund phrase counts as a subject that is not plural.
class_link.z3: All(s, [snorving, dramping, smoking, parting], Implies(gerund_phrase(s), non_plural(s)))

original: All(s, [snorving, dramping, smoking, parting], Implies(gerund_phrase(s), grammatical_number(s) == singular))

snorving.says: 'Snorve' is a verb, so 'snorving quietly at work' is a gerund phrase.

singular: Snorving quietly at work is frowned upon
plural: Snorving quietly at work are frowned upon

dramping.says: 'Dramp' is a verb, so 'dramping the dough twice' is a gerund phrase.

label_corrections.why: The verb's number is a functional link from the subject to one of two values (singular, plural), the DL file's takes_verb_form; choosing the sentence is choosing that value. No arithmetic and no comparison of two variable values.
